title: 5-Fold Cross-Validation for R^2 and RMSE
description: Use KFold(n_splits=5) and cross_val_score on the regression pipeline reg to report the mean and standard deviation of R^2 and RMSE across 5 folds.

steps.description: Create `kf = KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)` and run `cross_val_score` twice on `(reg, X, y)`: once with `scoring='r2'` and once with `scoring='neg_root_mean_squared_error'` (negated with `-` to recover positive RMSEs).
Print the 5-fold mean and standard deviation (`mean() ± std()`) for both `scores_r2` and `scores_rmse`.

Look at the leading minus sign on line 3: scikit-learn convention makes all scorer values higher-is-better, so `'neg_root_mean_squared_error'` returns negative numbers and `-cross_val_score(...)` flips them back to positive RMSEs.

steps.question: How many elements are in the array `scores_r2` returned by `cross_val_score(reg, X, y, cv=kf, scoring='r2')`?
steps.answer: 5 elements, one test-fold $R^2$ score for each of the 5 folds in `KFold(n_splits=5)`.

steps.description: Line 3 evaluates `reg` across all 5 folds and negates the returned array so `scores_rmse` holds the 5 positive RMSE values.
